examples.vi: Vui lòng thanh toán trước để giữ chỗ trong chuyến tham quan.

examples: My commissioners pay half of the price upfront and the other half after they receive the finished product.
wiktionary.gloss: Beforehand.

examples: He's a poor defender, so we always play him upfront.
wiktionary.gloss: As an attacker.

senses.definition: A presentation where TV networks sell advertising for a new season to major clients.

examples.en: The networks showcased their new shows at the upfront in New York.
examples.vi: Các hãng truyền hình giới thiệu chương trình mới tại buổi bán quảng cáo đầu mùa ở New York.

senses.vi: buổi bán quảng cáo đầu mùa

wiktionary.gloss: A meeting of network executives with the press and major advertisers, signaling the start of advertising sales for a new season.

senses.definition: To put something first so that people will consider it.

examples.en: She upfronted the cost issue at the start of the meeting.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đưa vấn đề chi phí lên đầu tiên ngay khi cuộc họp bắt đầu.

senses.vi: đưa lên hàng đầu; đưa ra trước để xem xét

wiktionary.gloss: To bring to the fore; to place up front for consideration.

blocks.etymology: From Late Latin valentia and Latin valentia (“bodily strength; health; vigour”) + English -y (suffix forming abstract nouns denoting a condition, quality, or state). Valentia is derived from valēns (“healthy, strong, vigorous”) + -ia (suffix forming feminine abstract nouns); while valēns is the present active participle of valeō (“to be healthy, sound, or well; to be strong; to have influence or power, etc.”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂welh₁- (“to rule; powerful, strong”). Sense 1 (“combining capacity of an atom”) and sense 3 (“number of arguments a verb can have”) are possibly from valence + -y.

thesaurus.definition: the phenomenon of forming chemical bonds
(biology) a relative capacity to unite or react or interact as with antigens or a biological substrate
(chemistry) a property of atoms or radicals; their combining power given in terms of the number of hydrogen atoms (or the equivalent)

Hoá trị.

examples: vaccine valency

The number of edges connected to a vertex in a graph.
